svg.title: Culturing microorganisms
svg.desc: BINARY FISSION: One bacterial cell divides into two by binary fission. With enough nutrients and a suitable temperature, division may occur every 20 minutes. Use the division time given in the question. 1 → 2 → 4 → 8: repeated doubling, not adding a fixed amount. Bacteria have no nucleus and do not divide by mitosis. GROWING A CULTURE: Nutrient broth supplies substances for growth. Agar gel plates provide a surface for colonies. A colony is a visible group grown from an initial cell or group of cells. An uncontaminated culture is needed to compare antimicrobial substances fairly. Aseptic technique prevents unwanted microorganisms entering. ASEPTIC TECHNIQUE: EQUIPMENT: Sterilise Petri dishes and medium before use → remove unwanted microorganisms. Sterilise the inoculating loop through a flame; let it cool before transfer → avoid contamination without killing the culture. Open the lid briefly → reduce entry of airborne microorganisms. Follow the school's handling and disposal procedure. ASEPTIC TECHNIQUE: PLATES: Secure the lid with small pieces of tape, not a complete seal → prevent accidental opening while allowing gas exchange. Store upside down → condensation does not drip onto the culture. Incubate school cultures at a maximum of 25°C → reduce the risk of growing harmful human pathogens. Do not open incubated plates. PRACTICAL: ANTIMICROBIAL DISCS: Prepare a bacterial lawn on sterile agar using aseptic technique. Place discs containing antiseptics or antibiotics onto the agar. Include a control disc with solvent only → check the solvent's effect. Incubate safely; measure the clear zones of inhibition. Repeat and calculate a mean for each substance. VARIABLES & CONCLUSIONS: Independent: substance tested, or its concentration. Dependent: inhibition-zone diameter or area. Keep strain, agar, disc size, substance volume, time and temperature constant. Larger zone suggests greater inhibition under these conditions. Different substances spread through agar differently; zone size alone cannot show which works best inside a patient. ZONE AREA: πr²: Measure across the clear zone → diameter. Radius = diameter ÷ 2. Diameter 12 mm → radius 6 mm. Area = π × 6² = 113 mm² (3 significant figures). Use squared units. Only subtract disc area if the question asks for the zone excluding the disc. A clear zone indicates growth was inhibited. POPULATION & STANDARD FORM: Number of doublings: n = total time ÷ division time. Final population = starting population × 2ⁿ. 50 bacteria; 20-minute division time; 2 hours: 120 ÷ 20 = 6 doublings; 50 × 2⁶ = 3,200. Standard form: 3.2 × 10³. Keep time units consistent; apply the stated growth conditions.

svg.text: Binary fission: one cell → two cells
